subject.title: fix(auth): bind OAuth and sessions to immutable identity

question: Should existing email-owned sessions and durable records be denied immediately on upgrade, or should the security hardening include an explicit reauthentication-based migration and recovery path?
rationale: Both options preserve the new immutable identity boundary differently, but only maintainers can choose the acceptable access-loss and operational-migration policy for deployed Crabbox instances.

options.title: Add explicit secure migration
options.body: Require a fresh GitHub OAuth login that proves the immutable account ID, then migrate only the matching legacy ownership through a narrow documented recovery path.

options.title: Accept immediate fail-closed cutover
options.body: Land the hard cutoff intentionally, with release/deployment guidance requiring operators to update admin owners and recreate or migrate affected records out of band.

recommendation.title: Add explicit secure migration
recommendation.body: Require a fresh GitHub OAuth login that proves the immutable account ID, then migrate only the matching legacy ownership through a narrow documented recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: A current-main feature-history owner is needed to choose the upgrade and recovery policy; the provided context does not establish a named owner.
